scale_007:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the initial setup of a {{vendor}} tenant for our company's SSO & access management rollout. This is a policy-gated step: creating the tenant issues root identity-provider admin credentials and a billing commitment, so a human (our IT/security lead) must explicitly authorize it before anything is submitted.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for any missing inputs you need: our company/organization name, our primary domain, preferred subdomain or tenant name for {{vendor}}, the admin email address to associate with the tenant, and which pricing/edition tier we intend to use.
2. Research and summarize {{vendor}}'s tenant creation process (signup/config form fields, required org details, available editions), and how its documented public API, Terraform provider (or equivalent), and directory REST APIs would let us later manage apps, groups, policies, and users as code — so I understand what we're committing to.
3. Draft a complete, ready-to-review setup plan: proposed tenant name/subdomain, admin email, edition/tier choice, and a checklist of what will be created (root admin account, billing plan, initial org settings). Note any security implications (root admin credential creation, billing commitment) clearly.
4. Pre-fill or draft the actual signup/configuration form values wherever possible, but do not submit the form, click confirm, accept any terms, or create the tenant yourself.
5. Present the completed draft and checklist to me for review, and explicitly stop for human sign-off — do not create root admin credentials or finalize billing on your own.

Report back with: the drafted tenant configuration, the checklist of what will be created, any open questions needing my input, and a clear statement that the plan is ready and awaiting my (or our IT/security lead's) explicit approval before you or I proceed to actually create the tenant.

scale_007:n2.prompt:
You are helping me define role-based access groups in {{vendor}}, our SSO/identity provider, as part of setting up SSO & access management across company tools. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (a) the list of company tools/apps we're connecting to {{vendor}}, (b) the roles or departments we need (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Finance, Admins, Contractors), (c) any known mapping of which roles should access which tools, and (d) confirmation that you have configured credentials to access our {{vendor}} tenant via its API or admin console.
2. Using the {{vendor}} directory's group management capabilities (API or dashboard), draft a proposed set of access groups—one per role/department—along with a description of intended membership rules (e.g., dynamic rules based on department attribute, or manual membership) and which apps/tools each group should be assigned to.
3. Do NOT create, apply, or push any groups, memberships, or app assignments yet. Only prepare a clear draft: a table or list showing group name, purpose, membership rule, and app assignments.
4. Check for conflicts or overlaps with any existing groups already in {{vendor}}, and flag anything ambiguous (e.g., users who could fit multiple roles) for me to resolve.
5. Summarize the draft plan back to me in plain text, including how each group maps to MFA and provisioning expectations if known.
6. After presenting the draft, stop for human sign-off — do not create or modify any groups, memberships, or assignments in {{vendor}} until I explicitly approve the plan.

Done looks like: a complete, reviewable draft of proposed role-based groups, their membership rules, and app assignments, with any conflicts flagged, and no changes yet applied to {{vendor}}. Report back with the full draft plan and a clear note that you are awaiting my approval before implementation.

scale_007:n3.prompt:
You are helping me configure Single Sign-On (SSO) applications in {{vendor}}, our identity provider, as part of rolling out company-wide SSO with role-based access and MFA. Approval is required before any changes go live, so you must prepare everything and then stop.

First, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} admin console/tenant URL and confirmation I have configured credentials available, (2) the list of company tools/apps we need to add for SSO (name, and whether each is in the {{vendor}} pre-built app catalog, needs custom SAML/OIDC setup, or requires header-based auth), and (3) any role/group mappings I want tied to each app.

Then, for each app: check whether it exists in the {{vendor}} catalog and note the standard integration path; for apps not in the catalog, outline the custom SAML/OIDC configuration steps using {{vendor}}'s documented walkthroughs (what metadata, certificates, or redirect URIs will be needed — do not invent specifics, note what must be gathered from each app's admin panel). Where relevant, note whether the app and its groups/policies can be defined as code via {{vendor}}'s Terraform provider (or equivalent) for reviewability, and draft that configuration as a proposal rather than applying it.

Produce a clear per-app checklist/summary: app name, integration method (catalog vs custom), required inputs still missing from me, and proposed role/group mapping. Do not create, enable, or push any live SSO app configuration, Terraform apply, or policy change — only prepare drafts and a summary.

Report back with the full checklist, any open questions or missing inputs, and then stop for human sign-off before I authorize applying any of these changes.

scale_007:n4.prompt:
You are helping me enable MFA policies in {{vendor}}, our SSO/identity provider, as part of our SSO & access management rollout. Approval requirement: a human must explicitly approve before any changes are applied — you must prepare everything but not apply or activate the policy.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing, such as: our {{vendor}} tenant/admin URL, the list of user groups and apps (especially sensitive apps needing stronger auth), and any existing conditional access requirements (trusted networks, managed devices, geo-restrictions).

Then, using your configured credentials, draft an MFA policy configuration in {{vendor}}'s admin console covering:
1. A baseline MFA requirement for all users, with authenticator app or push as default factors.
2. Passwordless sign-in options — enable and document support for passkeys and platform biometrics so employees can authenticate without a password where supported.
3. A stricter policy tier requiring FIDO2 security keys or passkeys specifically for sensitive apps or privileged groups (identify which apps/groups qualify based on what I tell you or reasonable defaults, and flag them for my confirmation).
4. Context-aware/conditional rules that factor in network, device trust, and location/risk signals to adjust authentication requirements per app or group.

Prepare the policy as a draft (not yet enabled/enforced) in the admin console, and produce a clear written summary: which groups/apps are covered, what factors are required per tier, and any conditional access rules configured. Include a checklist of what will change for end users (e.g., re-enrollment prompts, passkey setup steps).

Do not activate, enforce, or publish the policy — stop for human sign-off once the draft and summary are ready. Report back with the draft policy details, the summary, the checklist, and a clear note that the policy is staged pending my approval.

scale_007:n5.prompt:
You are helping me provision existing employees into {{vendor}}, our chosen SSO/identity platform, as part of setting up SSO & access management. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) my company domain, (2) the source of truth for existing employees (HRIS export, CSV, or existing directory), (3) the role/group mapping I want applied per user (e.g., department -> app/group), and confirmation that my {{vendor}} credentials are already configured for you to use.

Once I provide these, do the following:
1. Retrieve the current list of existing users already present in {{vendor}} (use the platform's documented user-listing endpoint or API, e.g. a users list call) so we know who's already provisioned.
2. Cross-reference that list against my HR/employee source to identify which users still need profiles created.
3. For each missing user, prepare a draft user profile: name, email, assigned role/group, and MFA enrollment requirement — using {{vendor}}'s user creation function or API in draft form only (do not submit yet).
4. Compile a clear summary table: users to be created, their proposed role/group, MFA status, and any data conflicts or duplicates you found.

Do not create, modify, or push any user profiles or provisioning workflows into {{vendor}} or any downstream app. This step requires a human to explicitly approve the batch before anything is applied — stop for human sign-off once your draft list and summary are ready.

Report back with: the reconciled list of users to provision, their proposed role/group and MFA settings, any discrepancies found, and confirm you are pausing for my approval before creation.

scale_007:n6.prompt:
You are helping me verify that Single Sign-On is working correctly across all company applications connected to our Okta or Google SSO setup. 

First, ask me for: (1) the list of company tools/apps that have SSO configured (e.g., Slack, Google Workspace, GitHub, Salesforce, AWS, etc.), (2) the SSO provider we use (Okta or Google), and (3) the login URL or dashboard where SSO authentication starts (e.g., the company's Okta or Google sign-in portal), and (4) confirmation that a test user account exists that I should log in as (do not ask me for its password — you will use your configured credentials).

Then, for each app in the list:
1. Navigate to the app's login page.
2. Confirm it redirects to the SSO provider's login flow rather than a native username/password form.
3. Complete authentication using your configured credentials.
4. Confirm the app loads successfully post-login and shows the correct authenticated user/session.
5. Check that MFA is prompted where expected during the flow.
6. Note any app where SSO fails, falls back to a local login, skips MFA, or throws an error.

Keep a running table with columns: App Name, SSO Redirect Success (Y/N), Login Success (Y/N), MFA Prompted (Y/N), Notes/Errors.

Done looks like: every app in the list has been tested and the table is complete, with clear pass/fail status and error details for any failures.

Report back with the full results table, a summary count of passes vs. failures, and specific details (error messages, screenshots if captured, or redirect URLs) for any app that failed, so I can follow up with IT or the app's admin console.

scale_007:n7.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the company-wide rollout of SSO (Okta or Google Workspace SSO) across our tools, with role-based access, MFA, and provisioning already configured in a staging/admin environment. This is a policy-gated step: a human (our IT/security lead) must explicitly approve before the rollout is applied to all users. Do not enable, push, or activate SSO/MFA enforcement for the broader team yourself.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: the list of integrated applications, the identity provider in use (Okta or Google Workspace), the defined roles/groups and their app access mappings, MFA policy details, and the target rollout groups/order (e.g., pilot group first, then full company).
2. Using your configured credentials, review the current SSO/admin configuration and compile a rollout readiness summary: which apps are connected, which roles/groups are mapped, MFA requirements, and any provisioning rules (auto-create/deactivate accounts).
3. Draft a rollout plan document including: rollout sequence (pilot vs. full), communication/notification text for employees (what changes, what they need to do, MFA enrollment steps), a rollback plan if issues arise, and a checklist of pre-rollout verification items (test logins, MFA enrollment test, provisioning test).
4. Flag any gaps or risks you find (e.g., apps not yet connected, roles missing MFA, users without assigned groups).
5. Compile all of this into a single readiness report with clear action items and open questions for the security lead.

Do not trigger the actual rollout, enforce MFA, or change any live user access or credentials. Once the readiness report and rollout plan are complete, stop for human sign-off — the security lead must explicitly authorize the company-wide rollout before it proceeds.

Report back with: the compiled readiness report, the rollout plan draft, the list of flagged risks/gaps, and confirmation that no changes were applied, pending approval.
